summary: B is the preferable patch because it keeps the change localized, reuses the multipart helper, shares request/response logic, and directly tests retries with streamed os.File content. Neither candidate fully follows the frozen contract.
reasons: B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and tests the multipart field, filename, content, and replay after a 429 using an open file.
B keeps retry handling out of the global RawClient, avoiding A's explicitly out-of-scope modification of unrelated request/retry machinery.
B centralizes option handling, request construction, and response decoding in add, whereas A duplicates the existing Add implementation inside Upload.
A changes retry and reader-ownership semantics for every seekable RawClient request and expands behavior to Files.Update, contrary to the contract's scope restrictions.
risks_a: Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request and response behavior.
The global enableBodyReplay machinery broadens the change beyond file uploads and mutates seekable readers through a shared GetBody closure.
It lacks a source-reader failure test, and its Upload retry test uses strings.Reader rather than the reported streamed os.File case.
risks_b: Add now eagerly buffers every custom multipart body, changing established memory, timing, and source-error semantics despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.
Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing FilesService.Add method required by the contract.
Tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader failure coverage.
